raw_response:
I will still plant all 10.1 mu with cotton. I have done cotton for many years, so I do not like making big changes unless I see it pays. Last year’s way is my base, then I adjust a little. With 10.1 mu, fertilizer and spray money matters, but if I cut too much and yield drops, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I have well water, so I will not let the field stay dry at the key stages. For seed, I will use an improved type, because around here the better-performing cotton seed usually comes out more even and gives a steadier stand than old saved seed. For fertilizer, I will keep nitrogen on the stronger side, because cotton needs strength to hold bolls, but I will also give phosphorus and potassium so it does not grow only stalk and leaves. I will prepare the land with ploughing first, because cotton likes a cleaner, looser seedbed, and I have seen better emergence that way than just scratching the surface. On insects and disease, I will not wait too long once pressure shows up, because one bad wave can cost a lot. If the weather is normal, I will aim for about 350 kg per mu of seed cotton. That is a level I feel is worth chasing without spending wildly.
